Some of Stonehenge's stones were dragged 225 km. 🪨 Watch 1,500 years of building in 26 seconds. ⏱️

Around 3000 BC it started as a simple circular ditch and bank. Then came the bluestones, up to 4 tons each, hauled about 225 km from the Preseli hills in Wales. Around 2500 BC the giants arrived: sarsens averaging ~25 tons, dragged ~32 km from the Marlborough Downs, raised into a 30-stone circle and five huge trilithons up to 10 m tall.

The twist: the lintels are locked on with mortise-and-tenon and tongue-and-groove joints. Carpentry joints, cut into solid stone.

How would YOU move a 25-ton stone? One word 👇

yt_description:
c. 3000 BC: circular ditch and bank with 56 holes. Bluestones (up to ~4 t) brought ~225 km from the Preseli hills, Wales. c. 2500 BC: sarsens (avg ~25 t) from the Marlborough Downs ~32 km away, raised as a 30-upright circle with lintels plus 5 trilithons (up to ~10 m, 45+ t). Lintels held with mortise-and-tenon joints; circle lintels joined tongue-and-groove. c. 2200 BC bluestones rearranged; activity to c. 1520 BC.

Sources: https://www.britannica.com/technology/How-Was-Stonehenge-Built · https://www.livescience.com/stonehenge-england-ancient-history
Figures are historical estimates. Stylised 3D animation.
